fatal_blockers: 1 — The jet fold supplies no explicit polynomial-time matrix or polynomial row bound. Coordinate order-q jets require exponentially many q-subsets, while the proposed q=3 ILP may inspect labeled fibers and overfit exactly as the killed sampled pure-power fold did; a fixed-q success would not address asymptotic soundness or arbitrary mixed words.

2 — Hankel minors are nonlinear functions of the selected columns and therefore are not syndrome rows. Explicit exterior coordinates reproduce the exponential determinant dictionary, while free linearized minor variables can fake consistency; using F17 also lacks the required binary rank and transfer accounting.

3 — A binary or integer lattice records additive combinations, not ordered nonabelian products. Fox derivatives depend on word prefixes, so direct evaluation is nonlinear in the selected triples; implementing those prefixes requires a tableau/circuit or witness dictionary, re-entering proved obstructions.

4 — Neither “isolated” nor the selector matrix is specified. If isolation uniquely identifies matchings, the sectors become complete-witness fingerprints and risk exponential size; if sectors remain additive, odd affine combinations and the already-observed branch splice remain cheap.

5 — Tropical leading-term selection is a nonlinear minimum operation, not a linear lattice constraint. Direct valuation rows retain signed cancellations, whereas explicit common-base monomials have factorial size and succinct circuit evaluation re-enters tableau faults.

6 — The Krawtchouk map is linear over F2, so every support-three affine trade survives it. If an illegal word is the XOR of three legal words of transformed cost at most B, its transformed cost is at most 3B, ruling out an N^c gap; useful uncompressed subset rows are also exponential.

7 — Linear boundary lattices cannot charge nonlinear Dehn area. The signed sum of three cheap legal fillings fills their illegal affine combination with only constant-factor norm increase, while enforcing positive combinatorial diagrams would require nonlinear or local-tableau constraints.
evidence: The frozen sampled pure-power experiment lost its initial ratio under larger families, dropping to one or below; the exact pure-power dimension theorem gives rank sum_{j<=r} binom(k,j). Thus proposal 1's q=3 optimization is not a discriminating asymptotic test.
The determinant/permutation verifier found short virtual states even after adding every compound coordinate, while explicit dictionaries remained factorial. This directly wounds proposals 2 and 5.

The exchange-quotient verifier found illegal odd covers in the affine span of perfect matchings in 32 instances. Any additive selector, holonomy feature, or filling representation must explicitly defeat this relation rather than merely relabel it.

The tested global selector/phase mutation admitted a weight-9 rectangle splice, and global feature shells achieved at best 7/6 versus the base 5/3. No proposed selector mechanism supplies a theorem escaping these attacks.

The bounded-local, marginal, and phase obstructions do not directly cover genuinely global jets or nonabelian products, but being outside those hypotheses is not positive evidence. The missing requirements are an explicit linear matrix, polynomial rank, witness-blind construction, and all-mixed-word soundness.
Exact syndrome-to-CVP transfer applies only after an explicit binary matrix is obtained. It cannot transfer nonlinear minors, tropical minima, group-word evaluation, or combinatorial filling area.
next_experiment: No implementation is justified as written. The only credible escape is proposal 1 mutated to an explicit, witness-blind, polynomial-time binary matrix J(H,t,q) with a proved polynomial row bound; then freeze that rule and exhaust every mixed word on bounded q=3 and q=4 tiny 3DM, all-eight, odd-holonomy, and relabeled instances, rejecting unless its worst-YES/best-NO ratio and output-rank exponent both beat the unfurled baseline. An ILP selecting rows from labeled YES/NO fibers does not count.
